<reason>A won a close, high-quality clash by making the proposition easier to decide: the file is the adoptee’s origin, the child never consented to secrecy, and optional contact does not justify a lifelong government blank. B was sharp on search-era identification and irreversibility, but never resolved the strain in “for the child” sealing later used against that same adult, and the pipeline/trust claims stayed speculative. A’s rights path and registry-as-veto frame did more work than B’s remaining harm story.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s first rebuttal: mutual-consent registries as “sealed records with a waiting room,” plus DNA already leaking so seals disable only the adoptee — undercutting both B’s middle path and the anonymity promise.</best_rebuttal>
